subject: Discovery recap: reserved LLM inference fit + next steps
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chu <alex@crescent.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 3 Aug 2025 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: reserved LLM inference fit + next steps

Alex — thanks for the time today. Quick recap from Redwood's side and the concrete next steps so we keep momentum. I wrote this up to capture the goals, pain, and what we proposed on the call.

Key pain and goals you shared
- Latency spikes during peak inference windows (tail p99 frequently beyond 600ms for short prompts).
- Mixed workload: low-latency customer chat plus batch scoring overnight (models range from 2k to 8k tokens).
- Data isolation requirement for PII-bearing prompts — legal wants dedicated tenancy and audit logs.
- Predictable cost: you need a committed unit price for 12-month procurement planning.

Redwood proposal summary (what we recommended)
- Reserved capacity: dedicated pool (reserved GPUs) sized for sustained baseline traffic (we estimated 8 A100-equivalent GPUs for steady throughput; burst to 12 for peak windows).
- Isolation: single-tenant pool with network segmentation + customer-managed VPC peering (SOC2-compatible controls; retention of audit logs for 13 months).
- SLO targets: 95/50ms p50, 95/180ms p95, 99/350ms p99 for typical short-chat prompts (payloads ~256 tokens). For long-sequence scoring we recommend a separate provisioning lane with higher throughput throughput-optimized instances.
- Cost controls: commit pricing + recommended batching & KV-prefix caching to reduce per-token cost by ~30% on non-real-time workloads.

Open questions we need answered to finalize sizing/pricing
1) Typical tokens-per-request distribution for chat vs batch (histogram or percentile numbers).
2) Required retention window and where logs must be stored (your security asked about EU-only storage for some datasets).
3) Any hard constraints on GPU family (e.g., you require on-prem A100 NVLINK vs cloud A100S) — affects procurement path.

Agreed next steps / owners
- Alex: share a short sample logs/export (anonymized) or token distribution by EOD Wed, Aug 6. (helps finalize the sizing model).
- Ben: provide a preliminary committed-pricing worksheet + SLA addendum draft by Tue, Aug 5. (attached: crescent_infra_requirements.xlsx)
- Marissa: schedule a 30-min technical deep-dive with your infra lead for week of Aug 11.
- Mateo: I will follow up with a draft Mutual Action Plan and a proposed reserved-capacity term sheet once Ben's pricing draft is ready.

Attachments referenced: crescent_infra_requirements.xlsx (worksheet with our baseline sizing model).

If this recap misstates anything, say so — otherwise we'll proceed against these asks. Thanks again — good call.

—

Alex — attaching a preliminary committed-pricing worksheet and an SLA addendum template. Highlights here so you don't have to dig in first:
- Baseline: 8 A100-equivalent GPUs reserved (12 sustained peak), monthly committed fee: $78,000/mo (discounts layered for 12/24 mo term).
- Burst: automatic elastic capacity to 12 GPUs with negotiated burst policy; billing only on consumed GPU-hours beyond baseline.
- SLO outline (formal text in SLA addendum): uptime 99.95% monthly; p99 request latency objective included with latency credits for breach; incident response 1-hour P1.
- Security: enclave-based isolation + KMS integration; we include audit log export to your S3 bucket daily.

Attachments: crescent_infra_requirements.xlsx (updated with pricing columns). redline_reservation_term.docx (SLA + term sheet).

Next proposed sync: Tue, Aug 5 10:00am PT — 30m to walk the table and procurement asks. If that works for your team please confirm and I'll send a calendar invite.
